expected_evidence: Ice-core oxygen-isotope (δ18O) abrupt-shift records (e.g., GISP2, NGRIP) marking onset of pronounced cooling
Varved/laminated glacial-lake sediment sequences (Lake Agassiz, Lake Ojibway, Champlain Sea) showing a shift in outflow drainage from the Mississippi corridor to the St. Lawrence valley
Marine sediment cores from the Gulf of St. Lawrence / Labrador Sea / northwest Atlantic showing a low-salinity/freshwater spike (planktonic foraminiferal δ18O excursion, IRD layer, meltwater cap)
Geomorphological evidence of a St. Lawrence outlet flood channel or spillway erosion feature dated to the proposed interval
Radiocarbon- or cosmogenic-nuclide-dated moraine/ice-margin retreat features correlating with the routing switch
Terrestrial pollen/lake-sediment cooling proxies in eastern North America and Europe synchronous with the event
Population-genetic bottleneck signals in North American megafauna or contemporaneous human groups (weak, indirect)
response.rationale: If a St. Lawrence meltwater-routing event triggered Younger Dryas-style cooling, the expected signature would be almost entirely geological/paleoclimatic: ice-core isotope excursions, glacial-lake varve/outflow-channel evidence, and marine sediment freshwater/IRD spikes. These proxy archives are exceptionally well-preserved and precisely dated (annual-resolution ice cores and varves), so detectability for this evidence class is genuinely high (geological ~0.6-0.65, astronomical/chronometric ~0.65-0.7 in the table), and absence of such signals would be meaningful rather than merely a preservation artifact. Material, genetic, linguistic, textual, and oral-tradition evidence are essentially irrelevant or undetectable at this time depth (textual=0, oral_tradition/linguistic near 0), so their absence carries no weight. The larger problem is chronological: as model-prior (unverified, from training knowledge, not from supplied evidence) the real Younger Dryas onset is dated to roughly 12,900 calendar years BP (~10,900 BCE) via well-replicated ice-core and varve chronologies — several millennia later than the stated interval of -20000 to -19001 (~20,000-19,000 years BP, i.e., Last Glacial Maximum). Because the diagnostic geological/astronomical archives for this exact question are highly detectable and heavily studied, an absence of a documented cooling/freshwater-routing event at ~20-19 kya is not well explained by poor preservation — it more likely reflects a date/label mismatch in the hypothesis itself rather than a detectability failure. I therefore blend the 'younger-dryas' and 'upper-paleolithic' geological/astronomical rows and slightly discount for the apparent chronological inconsistency, landing at 0.55 rather than treating this as a straightforward high-detectability confirmation opportunity.
